questions.text: With respect to use of Condition Variable (CV), note that in addition to the CV, the wait() call takes a mutex lock as its second argument. State the dynamics of wait( ) call and explain the reason behind involving mutex lock in this design. Also briefly state the need for using a while() loop for the predicate check in the calling of the wait() operation.
questions.answer:
The wait() on CV, puts the caller to sleep + releases the lock (atomically), otherwise how could another thread acquire the lock and change the state and/or signal it to wake up? Also if putting to sleep + releases the lock both is not done atomically then also there is a race condition so that is also taken care by this call. Before returning after being woken up, wait() re-acquires the lock, thus ensuring that anytime the waiting thread is running between the lock acquired at the beginning of the wait sequence and the lock release at the end, it holds the lock. This design of wait() call thus is very convenient for application use so that programmer need not worry about concurrency issues coming up.
When a condition variable is signaled to wake up a thread, it is removed from the wait queue but before that thread reacquires the mutex, another thread may be given CPU time (and potentially the mutex). As a result, the shared state may be updated before the waking up thread reacquires the mutex. Therefore, the thread must do another check when it actually acquires the mutex to ensure the condition it needs to proceed is still true.

questions.text: Briefly state four distinct reasons (or advantages) why modern OS support/implement memory virtualization.
questions.answer:
1) Efficient and easy abstraction to user as it free’s the application programs from having to manage shared memory space and leave to the OS the burden of managing it.
2) Better Protection due to memory isolation
3) Despite of protecting each process address space, once can share certain portions like code etc.
4) Being able to run processes even if they require more memory than might be physically available.

questions.text: Q4(a): How many virtual pages are fast pages?
questions.answer:
a) 4KB/4 = 1024 PTEs
1024/2 = 512 PTEs => 512 or (29) pages are fast

questions.text: Q4(b): How many virtual pages are normal pages?
questions.answer:
b) The remaining 512 PTEs refer to second-level page tables. Each second-level page table has 1024 PTEs, so:
29 * 210 = 219 pages are normal

questions.text: Q4(c): What is the maximum size of an address space in bytes (use exponential notation for convenience, e.g., 2^3)?
questions.answer:
c) The size of the address space is the total number of pages times the size of each page:
(29 + 219) * 212 = 221 + 231 bytes

questions.text: Q4(d): If TLB fetch time is T (with hit ratio as H) and Memory access time is M, what is the time taken for a memory reference (assume all referenced pages in memory) whose entry is in fast page?
questions.answer: d) EAT for fast pages = T*H+ (1-H)*(T+M) +M= T+ (2-H) *M

questions.text: Q4(e): If TLB fetch time is T (with hit ratio as H) and Memory access time is M, what is the time taken for a memory reference (assume all referenced pages in memory) whose entry is in normal page?
questions.answer: e) EAT for normal pages = T*H+ (1-H)*(T+2M) +M= T+ (3-2H) *M

questions.text:
Consider the following program:
  main(){
int fd; 
fd = open(“outfile”, O_CREAT|O_RDWR); // Line 1
fork(); // Line 2
write(fd, “hello”, 5);
exit(0);}
Assume that all system calls succeed on a uniprocessor system. Also, assume that a system call cannot be interrupted in the middle of its execution. What will be the contents of the “outfile” file, after all processes have successfully exited?
questions.answer:
hellohello 
Fork will create two processes with the same fd pointing to the given file. Two “hello” writes will be observed by the same fd (seek value or pos will be shared). And because of the given assumption, interleaving/mixing of these two writes is not possible.

questions.text: What will be the contents of “outfile” if fork() was called before open() i.e, Line 2 comes before Line 1 in the program (see comments for identifying Line 1 & 2) above.
questions.answer:
hello 
Value of fd will be same for both the process. But open file entry corresponding to both this fd are different. ie. there are two copies of write offset. After open system call, write offset in each of the opened file entry is initialized to zero. And second write will over write the first one.
